newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Volatile platinum seen testing resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Volatile platinum seen testing resistance.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 18--------------
Platinum is seen as the focus on Friday, with a tight market and nervy conditions possibly prompting tests of resistance around $384-$385, dealers and analysts said.
Gold and silver would take a back seat, but gold may have a go at the $345 level, they added.
PLATINUM -
A very tight physical market would continue to boost prices while uncertainty over supply from Russia would keep volatility high.
"There is a shortage of platinum and the market has gone into backwardation, which we haven't seen for a long time," a dealer in continental Europe said.
Spot prices surged to a high bid of $382.50 on Thursday and were hovering just under $380 early on Friday morning.
"It's very expensive to go short. I would think a test of the highs around $384 would be expected today," a London dealer said.

Chartists said the market was looking technically stronger after pushing back above a downtrend that began in May 1995. Resistance was pegged at $384 to $385, based on an area of congestion on the charts and a series of highs in early to mid-March.
A break above that would allow prices to move to $391.00 and $392.50, and within sight of the year's peak at $406.
Players would be wary, however, of any signs that big producer South Africa would jump in to increase supplies, dealers said. Support was seen around $365.
At 0825 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $379.00/380.00, up $2.50 from Thursday's New York close.
GOLD -
Players would be eyeing platinum, and another show of strength in that market might prompt a test of resistance of $345.

"Overall the market continued with its bout of shortcovering, but does not yet have enough momentum to go above $345. However, we suspect that it will peak above there today to try to shake out the weak shorts," said broker GNI in a commentary.
Gold was still damaged from the heavy selling by funds early in the week.
"The technical indicators have firmed in support of the bounce, though the metal has some way to go before signalling a recovery," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
Resistance at $345 was strengthened by the 10-day moving average just above that level. Support was pegged at $340 and then at Wednesday's low of $337.50 and the year's low of $336.15.
At 0740 GMT spot gold was quoted at $342.00/$342.50 down 30 cents from Thursday's New York close.
SILVER -
The market was giving a rollercoaster ride to participants, touching both ends of its range on Thursday around $4.85 and $4.65.
The market was likely to try to break one way or the other on Friday, but it was unclear which way, the European dealer said.

Above Thursday's high of $385, the market would have to confront $4.88, the high of April 3 and the ceiling of recent price activity. Above that area, there is only the psychological $5.00 area to stop prices from surging up to $5.06/7.
At 0740 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.72/4.74, unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
